messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert triggered: elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts on hosted-api /api/v1/generate (us-west). 1m error rate = 9.3%, baseline 0.7%. Backfills: multiple 502/504s + client timeouts. Pager routed to SRE oncall. Links: https://dash.internal/redwood/apps/hosted-api/errors?range=5m ; logs: https://logs.internal/q=redwood-gateway%20error

Maya (SRE): I'm on it. Can someone confirm whether this is ingress vs runtime? Any deploys in last 30m?

Ravi (Platform): No deploys from platform team in last 40m. NGINX-ingress scaled normally. I see a small spike of 502s hitting the gateway after ~1719004200.

Alice (Observability): quick note — traces for many failed requests have trace_id=null and no span ids. Looks like our log-forwarder dropped application logs for large payload requests. Sampling config shows a change 172h ago but nothing recently; however the log agent restarted in us-west about 8m ago (kube events show image: logs-agent:2.1.7 -> 2.1.8).

Jordan (CS): CS reported two paying customers (AcmeCorp, FinCo) seeing timeouts and partial responses. Acme raised a ticket: "requests hang ~30s then error". Need ETA for mitigation so we can update customers.

Maya (SRE): hypothesis: request path to model runtime is OK but observability gap makes it hard to correlate. First priority: restore traces/logs so we can see root cause. If that's slow, we do live mitigation (fallback routing to smaller model variant + extend client timeouts). Sam, you want to IC?

Sam (IC): I'm taking IC. Plan: 1) Try quick instrumentation/patch to restore logs/traces. 2) If logs can't be restored in 10m, roll traffic to model-variant-small for non-enterprise customers and pin enterprise customers to Dedicated nodes. 3) Customer comms via Jordan. Assignments: Alice -> temp logging patch; Ravi -> rollback/ingress tweaks; Maya -> live monitoring and rollback guardrails.

Alice (Observability): I can push a stopgap env patch to the gateway to force verbose request logging (bypass agent filter). Patch command: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/redwood-gateway FORCE_VERBOSE_LOG=true LOG_PAYLOAD=true
```
This will blow up log volume but should immediately surface payloads and trace ids. I also recommend bumping app-level tracing sample rate to 100% for 10m: 
```
kubectl -n prod patch deployment/redwood-gateway --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE","value":"1.0"}}]'
```
I'll watch ES indexing.

Ravi (Platform): On ingress: I can increase proxy timeout and change fallback rules. Running: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap nginx-ingress-controller --patch '{"data":{"proxy-read-timeout":"60","proxy-send-timeout":"60"}}'
```
Also preparing a small canary to drop the new logs-agent version (2.1.8 -> 2.1.7) in us-west if we confirm regressions.

Lena (DevEx): If we flip FORCE_VERBOSE_LOG will SDKs/clients see any behavior change? Also flagging potential PII — we should enable masking: set LOG_MASK_KEYS=\"authorization,credit_card,ssn\" while patching.

Alice (Observability): good call. I'll include LOG_MASK_KEYS. Full patch I'll apply in 30s and post results.

incident-bot: Action required: oncall acknowledged. Incident status -> investigating. Current assignees: Sam (IC), Maya (SRE), Alice (Observability), Ravi (Platform). Priority: P1.

Maya (SRE): Applying ingress timeout bump now. Monitoring GWs.

Alice (Observability): Pushed env vars to redwood-gateway in us-west: `FORCE_VERBOSE_LOG=true`, `LOG_PAYLOAD=true`, `LOG_MASK_KEYS=authorization,credit_card,ssn`, `TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0`. Initial logs show trace_id present for ~40% of previously null requests. Seeing payloads for many 502s — e.g. 
```
[gateway] request_id=abcd1234 trace_id=efgh5678 model=llama-13b seq=1 err="upstream timeout"
```

Ravi (Platform): Good. I'm seeing a queue backlog on runtime pool for llama-13b; some workers returning 504s under load. Could be KV cache saturation — redis P95 latency jumped from 5ms -> 320ms.

Maya (SRE): is redis shard healthy? Anyone touching K/V or cache config?

Ravi (Platform): No config changes. Looking at Redis metrics: memory spikes and some evictions. Might be cache hotkeying for some prefixes after recent user activity patterns.

Sam (IC): Mitigations: 1) divert non-enterprise traffic to model-variant-small (llama-7b) to reduce runtime pressure. 2) temporarily disable KV-prefetch for hosted-api route. Ravi/Maya implement both. 3) Alice continue to monitor traces for root cause signals. Jordan craft two-line customer updates.

Ravi (Platform): rolling traffic rule now: `route /api/v1/generate -> split(enterprise:100%->llama-13b, public:100%->llama-7b)` applying via gateway config manager. Applying canary to 5% first.

Maya (SRE): also disabling KV prefetch flag on gateway (env: KV_PREFETCH=false) to reduce redis load. Patching now.

Alice (Observability): tracing quality improved after env patch; we have full spans for ~85% of failed requests now. Correlation shows most 5xx/504s have high redis latency preceding the RPC to model runtime. Sample stack: gateway -> kv-cache -> runtime-proxy -> model-worker timeout.

Jordan (CS): Messaging: "We're aware of elevated errors/timeouts in US-WEST affecting generation for some customers. We're rolling emergency mitigations to reduce impact and will update in 30 minutes. For impacted customers we've opened priority tickets." /cc @Nina

Nina (Product): please include note on which customers were shifted to fallback model and whether quality/regression tradeoffs are expected. We need to approve before forcing on enterprise tenants.

Sam (IC): enterprise stays on llama-13b for now; public traffic to 7b can be lower quality but restores availability. If enterprise requests want preserved capacity, we can spin dedicated workers.

Ravi (Platform): canary at 5% -> logs show reduced queue times in that shard. Rolling to 50% now.

Maya (SRE): KV_PREFETCH=false live. Redis p95 dropped to 18ms, evictions stabilized. Gateway 5xx rate dropped to 1.2% from 9.3% over 10m window. Good signal.

Alice (Observability): closing loop on missing telemetry root cause: logs-agent 2.1.8 had an aggressive payload filter that dropped application logs > 512kb. That caused null trace IDs in the pipeline and hampered debugging. File issue and revert plan in platform backlog.

Sam (IC): Recovery path looks good. Next: 1) schedule revert of logs-agent 2.1.8 in us-west after verification window. 2) create permanent guard: alert if trace_id=null > 5% of requests. 3) post-incident action items: improve canary checks for logs-agent, add KV prefetch circuit breaker.

Jordan (CS): notifying AcmeCorp/FinCo: "We deployed mitigations; you may see reduced quality as we route to fallback models, but service should be restored. We'll follow up with postmortem."

Maya (SRE): handing over to daytime oncall (Ravi) in 25 minutes. I'll remain reachable for 1h for followup.

Sam (IC): Handoff summary (for next oncall): incident id I-1719004321, impact: US-WEST hosted-api elevated 5xx due to redis/KV hotkeying and logs-agent filtering removing traces. Mitigation: env-patch to restore logs/traces, KV_PREFETCH disabled, public traffic routed to llama-7b, ingress timeouts bumped. Current status: degraded -> recovering, error rate ~1.1%. Next steps: platform to revert logs-agent or pin to 2.1.7 after canary, SRE to add trace_id null alert, product/CS to send official customer update.

Ravi (Platform): taking daytime oncall. I'll follow up on revert plan and postmortem notes.

incident-bot: Incident I-1719004321 status -> recovery. Pager cleared.

Sam (IC): closing thread — great work. Postmortem owners: Ravi (root cause + deploy processes), Alice (observability gap + checks), Maya (operational runbook for KV prefetch circuit breaker), Jordan (customer comms). I'll open retrospective doc. :tada:
